claims.text: The ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can accurately calculate the melting properties of refractory materials.
Machine-learning-based interpolation can reduce the computational cost of the ab initio free-energy approach.
The material is solid at standard temperature and pressure.
The proposed calculation is performed under constant-pressure and constant-temperature conditions.
Electronic structure and lattice vibrations mediate the calculation of melting properties.
The method uses thermodynamic integration with ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Machine-learning interpolation reduces the computational cost of thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics.
The predicted melting temperature will be within 10% of the experimental value.
The predicted entropy of fusion will be within 5% of the experimental value.
The predicted enthalpy of fusion will be within 5% of the experimental value.
The predicted volume change at the melting point will be within 2% of the experimental value.
The proposed method applies to refractory materials with melting temperatures above 2000 K.
The accuracy of the machine-learning interpolation scheme may affect the predicted melting properties.
The choice of DFT exchange-correlation functional may affect the predicted melting properties.
